en.title: Fresh snow in the US West: 13 in in 72 hours at Mt Baker (7 November)
en.description: Mt Baker got 13 in (32 cm) of new snow in the last 72 hours, 1 in (3 cm) of it in the last 24 hours. It now has about 17 in (44 cm) on its upper …
en.lede: Mt Baker got 13 in (32 cm) of new snow in the last 72 hours, 1 in (3 cm) of it in the last 24 hours. It now has about 17 in (44 cm) on its upper slopes, according to our snow model.

p: Elsewhere, Buttermilk, Monarch Mountain and Ski Cooper got 6 in (15 cm), 4 in (11 cm) and 4 in (11 cm) in the last 72 hours.
136 of 195 resorts in the US West have snow on their upper slopes today, and our model counts 74,363 sq mi (192,600 km²) of snow-covered ground.

The Chepeta station (10,489 ft / 3,197 m) measured 20 in (51 cm) of snow on the ground on 1 November, with 12 in (30 cm) of new snow in 24 hours. The Red Mountain Pass station (11,060 ft / 3,371 m) measured 24 in (61 cm) of snow on the ground on 1 November, with 11 in (28 cm) of new snow in 24 hours. The Bison Lake station (10,951 ft / 3,338 m) measured 15 in (38 cm) of snow on the ground on 1 November, with 10 in (25 cm) of new snow in 24 hours.
Keep in mind: resort values come from our snow model and describe an area, while stations measure one point.
Height matters: at Mt Baker, our model gives 8 in (21 cm) at the top (5,105 ft / 1,556 m), 4 in (11 cm) at mid-mountain (4,367 ft / 1,331 m) and 1 in (2 cm) at the base (3,629 ft / 1,106 m).
At Mt Baker, the freezing level reaches 5,971 ft (1,820 m) to 9,252 ft (2,820 m) on 7 November, above the top of the resort (5,105 ft / 1,556 m): rain or wet snow is possible on every slope that day.
Until 10 November, our forecast gives 21 in (53 cm) at Mt Baker.
Forecasts a few days ahead can change: look at the map again the day before you travel.
After fresh snow, wind builds drifts on sheltered slopes. Off-piste, the first days after a snowfall need the most care.

advice: Fresh snow is best in the first hours after it stops: go early, before the sun and the crowds.
Look for snow high up and on north-facing slopes: they keep it longest, while south-facing slopes lose it first in the sun.
Before you ski off-piste or go touring, read the official avalanche bulletin (links below).
Snow on the map does not mean a resort is open: check lifts and opening dates on the resort's website.
Get a powder alert in the SnowScope app to know when Mt Baker gets fresh snow.
